findings.issue: gate_entry_shape_problem reads a whole entry as one command, never splitting on && || ; |. Probed read-only: 'python3 a/test_x.py && python3 a/test_y.py' (two suites run in sequence, a correct entry, and the same joiner the plan's own lint gate uses) is reported as 'runs a/test_x.py as a program and hands it a/test_y.py as arguments' - a false statement - and would be refused by add, add --from-file, scope --gate and --gate-set and warned on by validate. No test covers a chained entry (gx1 quiet list has none).
findings.resolution: Cut the shell words at control operators before reading, judge each segment on its own (first path, the word before it, the extra suite paths), and add a chained-suites allow case to gx1.

findings.issue: The 'names a path twice' rule applies to every path-shaped word, not to suites. Probed: 'pytest a/test_x.py::t1 a/test_x.py::t2' (two distinct node ids) and 'python3 tools/r.py --in docs/p.json --out docs/p.json' are both refused/warned as naming a path more than once. The task says an entry naming one suite twice; an in-place tool invocation or two node ids of one file are legitimate and would be refused with no way round.
findings.resolution: Restrict the repeat rule to is_suite_path words and compare them with any '::' node id kept (or only flag when the whole word is identical); add an allow case for node ids and for a non-suite repeated path.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: acceptance (3) and tests.add say validate-manifest reports such an entry 'already in a plan' / 'a plan already holding a malformed gate entry' as a warning; the walk warns only for a task whose status is not TERMINAL, and gx2 pins silence for a done task. A plan holding the shape in finished tasks (the very tasks the fault was filed on) validates silent. The narrowing is the executor's own reading and the comment justifies it, but the clause does not carry it.
findings.resolution: Warn for every task regardless of status (it is only a warning), or get the clause amended before narrowing; drop the done-task half of gx2 accordingly.

findings.issue: 'Run as a program' is read from the word IMMEDIATELY before the first path, so an interpreter option hides it: 'python3 -u a/test_x.py a/test_y.py' and 'python3 -X dev a/test_x.py a/test_y.py' return None (probed) although they have exactly the F720 shape. The predicate's own docstring claims the interpreter-or-nothing reading.
findings.resolution: Walk back from the first path to the segment start, skipping option words (and their values), and treat '-m <module>' as a runner; add the option case to gx1.

It adds gate_entry_shape_problem beside gate_entry_paths, _gate_write_refusal in add/add --from-file/scope/retarget, _manifest_beside_gate_set for the trailing manifest and the swapped scope <manifest> <id>, and a warning in the phases walk. Diverges on the warning: 'a plan already holding a malformed gate entry draws a warning' became 'only for a non-terminal task' (finding 3); the warning lives in _manifest_phases._walk_phases, which _manifest_rules re-exports, so the clause's file is satisfied through delegation. The executor's claim ('no code changed this run', earlier implementation = predicate, write-verb refusals, --gate-set handling, warning) describes the diff accurately. On the asked judgement calls: the interpreter-word requirement does keep test runners (pytest, node --test, python3 -m pytest) quiet, but it reads only the immediately preceding word (finding 4) and does not split on && (finding 1). _manifest_beside_gate_set's swap needs the first positional to be an existing JSON plan with a phases list while the second is not; a task or phase id never is, so I found no real mis-route (the file tests are cwd-relative while the refusal also tries project-relative, which only ever errs toward refusing). F737 and sc4 not charged.
